authors: Guanghui Wang, Umar Syed, Robert E. Schapire, Jacob Abernethy

context: 6. Conclusion and Future Work In this paper, we studied multi-distribution learning, and introduced approximate lex-min-max optimality as the performance metric. Unlike min-max optimality, which focuses only on the worstcase group, lex-min-max optimality considers all groups in a lexicographic order. We showed that this objective can be achieved with similar ease as min-max optimality, by simply solving a regularized min-max game. Our paper takes a first step toward understanding full-distributions aware performance   guarantees 1 in MDL and raises several open questions. First, we do not know whether the O log T convergence rate of our algorithm can be improved, or whether a matching lower bound can be established. Second, it is important to validate the proposed methods with more empirical experiments. 12 L EXICOGRAPHIC M ULTI - DISTRIBUTION L EARNING
